articles.title: 完型 · 传播技术的演变
articles.context: 把印刷、报纸与电子传播放回历史进程中理解。先铺陈时间线，再突出计算机带来的变化；复杂处自然稍缓，不采用教学慢速。完型已依据可追溯答案还原，选项不进入阅读页面。
rows: Comparisons were drawn between the development of television in the 20th century |and the diffusion of printing in the 15th and 16th centuries.
人们曾把20世纪电视的发展与15、16世纪印刷术的传播相比较。
然而，在这两者之间的漫长岁月里，还发生了许多事情。

As was discussed before, it was not until the 19th century that the newspaper became the dominant pre-electronic medium, |following in the wake of the pamphlet and the book and in the company of the periodical.
如前所述，直到19世纪，报纸才成为电子传播时代到来之前的主导媒介；它继小册子和书籍之后兴起，并与期刊相伴发展。

It was during the same time that the communications revolution speeded up, |beginning with transport, the railway, and leading on through the telegraph, the telephone, radio, and motion pictures |into the 20th-century world of the motor car and the air plane.
也正是在这一时期，传播革命加快了步伐：从交通运输、铁路开始，继而经过电报、电话、广播和电影，一路迈入以汽车和飞机为标志的20世纪。
Not everyone sees that process in perspective.
并不是每个人都能从历史全局来看待这一进程。
It is important to do so.
而这样看待它，十分重要。

It is generally recognized, however, that the introduction of the computer in the early 20th century, |followed by the invention of the integrated circuit during the 1960s, radically changed the process, |although its impact on the media was not immediately apparent.
不过，人们普遍认为，20世纪初计算机的问世，以及随后在20世纪60年代集成电路的发明，彻底改变了这一进程，尽管它对传媒的影响并未立即显现。
As time went by, computers became smaller and more powerful, |and they became “personal” too, as well as institutional, |with display becoming sharper and storage capacity increasing.
随着时间推移，计算机体积越来越小，功能越来越强；除了供机构使用之外，也开始为个人所用，同时显示更清晰，存储容量也不断增大。
They were thought of, like people, in terms of generations, |with the distance between generations much smaller.
人们像划分人的世代一样，把计算机也划分为一代又一代，只不过两代之间的时间间隔要短得多。
It was within the computer age that the term “information society” began to be widely used |to describe the context within which we now live.
正是在计算机时代，“信息社会”这一术语开始被广泛用来描述我们如今所处的环境。

The communications revolution has influenced both work and leisure and how we think and feel both about place and time, |but there have been controversial views about its economic, political, social and cultural implications.
传播革命不仅影响了工作与休闲，也影响了我们对空间和时间的思考与感受；但对于它在经济、政治、社会和文化上的影响，人们一直存在争议。
人们不断权衡它带来的“益处”与“有害”后果。
而事实证明，要作出概括性的结论并不容易。

articles.title: 阅读一 · 如何恰当地运用幽默
articles.context: 像面对面分享演讲经验。叙述本身也有重点和起伏；天堂故事先舒展铺垫，到插队动作加快，再克制地落下笑点。主讲人05、新来者12、圣彼得13，不能靠频繁换声代替韵律。
rows: If you intend using humor in your talk to make people smile, |you must know how to identify shared experiences and problems.
如果你想在讲话中运用幽默，让听众会心一笑，就得懂得如何找出大家共有的经历和问题。
Your humor must be relevant to the audience |and should help to show them that you are one of them or that you understand their situation and are in sympathy with their point of view.
你的幽默必须与听众相关，并应让他们感到：你和他们是一路人，或者你了解他们的处境，也认同他们的看法。
Depending on whom you are addressing, the problems will be different.
听众不同，所涉及的问题也会不同。

If you are talking to a group of managers, you may refer to the disorganized methods of their secretaries; |alternatively if you are addressing secretaries, you may want to comment on their disorganized bosses.
如果你面对的是一群经理，可以谈谈他们的秘书做事如何缺乏条理；反过来，如果听众是秘书，你就不妨说说他们那些办事杂乱无章的上司。
Here is an example, which I heard at a nurses’ convention, |of a story which works well because the audience all shared the same view of doctors.
下面这个故事是我在一次护士大会上听来的。它之所以效果很好，是因为在场听众对医生都有着同样的看法。
A man arrives in heaven and is being shown around by St. Peter.
一个人来到天堂，圣彼得正领着他四处参观。
He sees wonderful accommodations, beautiful gardens, sunny weather, and so on.
他看到的是舒适的住处、美丽的花园、晴朗的天气，等等。

Everyone is very peaceful, polite and friendly |until, waiting in a line for lunch, the new arrival is suddenly pushed aside by a man in a white coat, |who rushes to the head of the line, grabs his food and stomps over to a table by himself.
人人都平和、礼貌而友善。可就在这位新来者排队领午餐时，一个穿白大褂的人突然把他推到一旁，冲到队伍最前面，抓起食物，重重地迈着步子，独自走到一张桌子旁。
“Who is that?” |the new arrival asked St. Peter.
“Oh, that’s God,” |came the reply, |“but sometimes he thinks he’s a doctor.”
“哦，那是上帝，”圣彼得回答，“不过，他有时以为自己是个医生。”

If you are part of the group which you are addressing, |you will be in a position to know the experiences and problems which are common to all of you |and it’ll be appropriate for you to make a passing remark about the inedible canteen food or the chairman’s notorious bad taste in ties.
如果你本就是听众中的一员，你自然了解大家共有的经历和问题；这时，顺口调侃一下食堂难以下咽的饭菜，或是那位会长挑领带时出了名的糟糕品味，就很合适。
With other audiences you mustn’t attempt to cut in with humor |as they will resent an outsider making disparaging remarks about their canteen or their chairman.
可面对其他群体的听众，就不要贸然拿这些事开玩笑，因为他们会反感一个外人对自己的食堂或会长说三道四。
You will be on safer ground if you stick to scapegoats like the Post Office or the telephone system.
把调侃对象限定在邮局、电话系统这类常被拿来出气的机构上，就稳妥多了。
If you feel awkward being humorous, you must practice so that it becomes more natural.
如果你讲起幽默来觉得别扭，就必须练习，让它逐渐变得自然。
Include a few casual and apparently off-the-cuff remarks |which you can deliver in a relaxed and unforced manner.
可以穿插几句随意、听来像是即兴想到的话，用轻松、不做作的方式说出来。
Often it’s the delivery which causes the audience to smile, |so speak slowly and remember that a raised eyebrow or an unbelieving look may help to show that you are making a light-hearted remark.
逗笑听众的，往往是表达方式。因此，讲话不妨从容些；还要记住，挑一挑眉，或露出不敢相信的神情，都能帮助听众明白：你是在轻松地开个玩笑。
It often comes from the unexpected.
幽默往往来自出人意料之处。
A twist on a familiar quote “If at first you don’t succeed, give up” |or a play on words or on a situation.
比如，把熟悉的名言稍作改动，变成“如果一开始没成功，那就放弃吧”；或者玩个文字游戏，或者借某种情境开个玩笑。
找找可以夸张或轻描淡写的地方。
Look at your talk and pick out a few words or sentences which you can turn about and inject with humor.
看看你的讲话内容，挑出几个词或几句话，稍加变化，为它们注入幽默。

articles.title: 阅读二 · 机器人与人的感知
articles.context: 从熟悉的机器讲到真正智能的难点。列举能力时轻快自然，转入常识、感知与筛选信息时突出逻辑反差；NASA引语由12号承担，主讲人保持05号。
rows: Since the dawn of human ingenuity, people have devised ever more cunning tools |to cope with work that is dangerous, boring, burdensome, or just plain nasty.
自人类开始展现创造才智以来，人们便不断设计出更巧妙的工具，去应对危险、枯燥、繁重，或纯粹令人厌恶的工作。
That compulsion has resulted in robotics—the science of conferring various human capabilities on machines.
正是这种强烈的需求催生了机器人学——一门将人的各种能力赋予机器的科学。
And if scientists have yet to create the mechanical version of science fiction, |they have begun to come close.
虽然科学家还没有造出科幻作品中那样的机器，但他们已经开始接近这一目标。
As a result, the modern world is increasingly populated by intelligent gizmos |whose presence we barely notice but whose universal existence has removed much human labor.
于是，现代世界里智能装置越来越多。我们几乎察觉不到它们的存在，但它们无处不在，已替人类省去了大量劳动。
Our factories hum to the rhythm of robot assembly arms.
在工厂里，机器装配臂有节奏地运转，发出阵阵嗡鸣。
Our banking is done at automated teller terminals that thank us with mechanical politeness for the transaction.
我们在自动柜员机上办理银行业务，交易结束后，机器还会机械而礼貌地向我们道谢。
Our subway trains are controlled by tireless robot-drivers.
我们的地铁列车由不知疲倦的机器人司机控制。

And thanks to the continual miniaturization of electronics and micro-mechanics, |there are already robot systems that can perform some kinds of brain and bone surgery with submillimeter accuracy—|far greater precision than highly skilled physicians can achieve with their hands alone.
而且，由于电子设备和微机械不断小型化，如今已有机器人系统能以亚毫米级的精度实施某些脑部和骨科手术——这远非技艺高超的医生单凭双手所能达到。

But if robots are to reach the next stage of laborsaving utility, |they will have to operate with less human supervision and be able to make at least a few decisions for themselves—|goals that pose a real challenge.
但是，机器人若要在节省人力方面更进一步，就必须在更少的人为监督下工作，并至少能够自主作出一些决定——这些目标构成了真正的挑战。

“While we know how to tell a robot to handle a specific error,” |says Dave Lavery, manager of a robotics program at NASA, |“we can't yet give a robot enough ‘common sense’ to reliably interact with a dynamic world.”
美国国家航空航天局一个机器人项目的负责人戴夫·拉弗里说：“尽管我们知道如何指示机器人处理某个特定错误，却还无法赋予它足够的‘常识’，让它可靠地应对不断变化的世界。”
Indeed the quest for true artificial intelligence has produced very mixed results.
的确，对真正人工智能的探索，取得的结果一直有喜有忧。

Despite a spell of initial optimism in the 1960s and 1970s |when it appeared that transistor circuits and microprocessors might be able to copy the action of the human brain by the year 2010, |researchers lately have begun to extend that forecast by decades if not centuries.
20世纪60年代和70年代，研究者起初曾一度乐观，认为到2010年，晶体管电路和微处理器或许就能模拟人脑的活动；但近来，他们已开始把这一预期向后推迟几十年，甚至几百年。

What they found, in attempting to model thought, is that the human brain's roughly one hundred billion nerve cells are much more talented—|and human perception far more complicated—than previously imagined.
研究者在尝试模拟思维时发现，人脑中约一千亿个神经细胞的能力远比先前想象的强大，而人的感知也远比先前想象的复杂。
They have built robots that can recognize the error of a machine panel by a fraction of a millimeter in a controlled factory environment.
他们已经造出机器人，能够在受控的工厂环境中识别机器面板上不足一毫米的误差。

But the human mind can glimpse a rapidly changing scene and immediately disregard the 98 percent that is irrelevant, |instantaneously focusing on the monkey at the side of a winding forest road or the single suspicious face in a big crowd.
而人只需瞥一眼迅速变化的场景，就能立即忽略其中98%的无关信息，瞬间将注意力集中到蜿蜒林间小路旁的猴子，或茫茫人群中那一张可疑的面孔上。
The most advanced computer systems on Earth can't approach that kind of ability, |and neuroscientists still don’t know quite how we do it.
地球上最先进的计算机系统也无法接近这种能力，而神经科学家至今仍不十分清楚，我们究竟是怎样做到的。

articles.title: 阅读三 · 油价冲击为何不同
articles.context: 以一个带担忧的反问开场，再像日常讨论经济问题那样逐层解释。区分旧冲击与新条件、富裕经济体与新兴经济体；数字服务比较，不念成新闻播报。
rows: Could the bad old days of economic decline be about to return?
经济衰退的苦日子，难道又要回来了吗？
Since OPEC agreed to supply-cuts in March, |the price of crude oil has jumped to almost $26 a barrel, up from less than $10 last December.
自石油输出国组织在3月同意减产以来，原油价格已从去年12月的每桶不足10美元，跃升至近26美元。
This near-tripling of oil prices calls up scary memories of the 1973 oil shock, when prices quadrupled, |and 1979-1980, when they also almost tripled.
油价近乎涨到原来的三倍，勾起了人们对两次石油危机的可怕记忆：1973年，油价涨到原来的四倍；1979至1980年，油价也几乎涨到原来的三倍。
Both previous shocks resulted in double-digit inflation and global economic decline.
此前的两次冲击，都导致了两位数的通货膨胀和全球经济衰退。
So where are the headlines warning of gloom and doom this time?
那么，这一次，那些预警经济前景黯淡、灾难将至的新闻标题怎么不见了？
The oil price was given another push up this week when Iraq suspended oil exports.
本周，伊拉克暂停石油出口，又推动油价向上走了一步。
Strengthening economic growth, at the same time as winter grips the northern hemisphere, |could push the price higher still in the short term.
经济增长势头增强，又逢北半球进入严冬，短期内可能进一步推高油价。
Yet there are good reasons to expect the economic consequences now to be less severe than in the 1970s.
不过，我们有充分理由认为，如今的经济后果不会像20世纪70年代那样严重。
In most countries the cost of crude oil now accounts for a smaller share of the price of petrol than it did in the 1970s.
在多数国家，与20世纪70年代相比，如今原油成本在汽油价格中所占的比重更小。
In Europe, taxes account for up to four-fifths of the retail price, |so even quite big changes in the price of crude have a more muted effect on pump prices than in the past.
在欧洲，税收占汽油零售价的比重高达五分之四，因此，即使原油价格出现较大变动，对加油站售价的影响也比过去小得多。
Rich economies are also less dependent on oil than they were, |and so less sensitive to swings in the oil price.
富裕经济体对石油的依赖也不像过去那么强，因而对油价波动也不那么敏感。
Energy conservation, a shift to other fuels and a decline in the importance of heavy, energy-intensive industries |have reduced oil consumption.
节约能源、转向其他燃料，以及高耗能重工业地位的下降，共同减少了石油消耗。
Software, consultancy and mobile telephones use far less oil than steel or car production.
软件、咨询和移动通信所消耗的石油，远少于钢铁或汽车生产。
For each dollar of GDP (in constant prices) rich economies now use nearly 50% less oil than in 1973.
按不变价格计算，如今富裕经济体每创造一美元的国内生产总值，所消耗的石油比1973年减少了近50%。

The OECD estimates in its latest Economic Outlook that, |if oil prices averaged $22 a barrel for a full year, compared with $13 in 1998, |this would increase the oil import bill in rich economies by only 0.25-0.5% of GDP.
经济合作与发展组织在最新一期《经济展望》中估计，如果全年平均油价达到每桶22美元，而1998年为13美元，那么富裕经济体新增的石油进口支出，也仅相当于其国内生产总值的0.25%至0.5%。
That is less than one-quarter of the income loss in 1974 or 1980.
这一损失还不到1974年或1980年收入损失的四分之一。
On the other hand, oil-importing emerging economies—to which heavy industry has shifted—|have become more energy-intensive, and so could be more seriously squeezed.
另一方面，那些需要进口石油的新兴经济体，由于承接了转移而来的重工业，能源消耗强度已经上升，因此可能受到更严重的挤压。

One more reason not to lose sleep over the rise in oil prices is that, |unlike the rises in the 1970s, it has not occurred against the background of general commodity-price inflation and global excess demand.
还有一个不必为油价上涨而失眠的理由：与20世纪70年代不同，这一次油价上涨并不是发生在大宗商品价格普遍上涨、全球需求过剩的背景下。
A sizable portion of the world is only just emerging from economic decline.
世界上相当大一部分地区才刚刚开始走出经济衰退。
The Economist’s commodity price index is broadly unchanging from a year ago.
《经济学人》的大宗商品价格指数与一年前相比，基本没有变化。
In 1973 commodity prices jumped by 70%, and in 1979 by almost 30%.
而在1973年，大宗商品价格曾上涨70%；1979年的涨幅也接近30%。

articles.title: 阅读四 · 临终照护与医疗责任
articles.context: 这是历史试卷中的医疗伦理讨论，不是现实医疗建议。用有温度但克制的解释语气，清楚区分意图与风险、镇痛与延长痛苦。乔治·安纳斯的直接引语使用13号，其余保持主讲05号。
rows: The Supreme Court’s decisions on physician-assisted suicide carry important implications |for how medicine seeks to relieve dying patients of pain and suffering.
最高法院关于医生协助自杀的裁决，对医学界应如何减轻临终患者的疼痛与痛苦，具有重要意义。

Although it ruled that there is no constitutional right to physician-assisted suicide, |the Court in effect supported the medical principle of “double effect,” |a centuries-old moral principle holding that an action having two effects—a good one that is intended and a harmful one that is foreseen—|is permissible if the actor intends only the good effect.
尽管法院裁定，宪法并未赋予人们接受医生协助自杀的权利，但它实际上支持了医学上的“双重效应”原则。这一已有数百年历史的道德原则认为：某项行为即使会产生两种效果——一种是有意追求的良好效果，另一种是可以预见的有害效果——只要行为者意在实现的仅是良好效果，该行为便是可以允许的。
Doctors have used that principle in recent years to justify using high doses of morphine to control terminally ill patients’ pain, |even though increasing dosages will eventually kill the patient.
近年来，医生援引这一原则，为使用大剂量吗啡控制绝症患者的疼痛提供正当依据，尽管不断增加剂量最终会导致患者死亡。

Nancy Dubler, director of Montefiore Medical Center, contends that the principle will shield doctors |who “until now have very, very strongly insisted that they could not give patients sufficient medication to control their pain if that might hasten death”.
蒙蒂菲奥里医疗中心主任南希·达布勒认为，这一原则将为医生提供保护；这些医生“直到现在还极其坚决地认为，如果用药可能加速死亡，他们就不能给予患者足够的药物来控制疼痛”。

George Annas, chair of the health law department at Boston University, maintains that, |as long as a doctor prescribes a drug for a legitimate medical purpose, |the doctor has done nothing illegal even if the patient uses the drug to hasten death.
波士顿大学卫生法系主任乔治·安纳斯坚持认为，只要医生开药是出于正当的医疗目的，那么即使患者使用该药来加速死亡，医生也没有违法。
“We don’t call those deaths homicides because the doctors didn’t intend to kill their patients, |although they risked their death.
“我们不会把那些死亡称为他杀，因为医生并无杀死患者的意图，尽管他们冒了患者可能死亡的风险。
If you’re a physician, you can risk your patient’s suicide as long as you don’t intend their suicide.”
如果你是一名医生，只要你并非有意促成患者自杀，就可以承担患者可能自杀的风险。”

On another level, many in the medical community acknowledge that the assisted-suicide debate |has been fueled in part by the despair of patients for whom modern medicine has prolonged the physical agony of dying.
从另一个层面看，医学界许多人承认，关于协助自杀的争论，部分源于患者的绝望：对这些患者而言，现代医学延长了临终过程中的肉体折磨。
Just three weeks before the Court’s ruling on physician-assisted suicide, |the National Academy of Science (NAS) released a two-volume report, Approaching Death: Improving Care at the End of Life.
就在法院就医生协助自杀作出裁决的三周前，美国国家科学院发布了一份两卷本报告，题为《走近死亡：改善生命末期的照护》。
Improving Care at the End of Life

It identifies the undertreatment of pain and the aggressive use of “ineffectual and forced medical procedures |that may prolong and even dishonor the period of dying” as the twin problems of end-of-life care.
报告指出，临终照护存在两大问题：一是疼痛治疗不足，二是过度采用“无效且强行实施的医疗措施，这些措施可能延长临终过程，甚至使这一过程失去尊严”。

The profession is taking steps to require young doctors to train in hospices, |to test knowledge of aggressive pain management therapies, to develop a Medicare billing code for hospital-based care, |and to develop new standards for assessing and treating pain at the end of life.
医学界正采取措施，要求年轻医生在临终关怀机构接受培训，考查他们对积极镇痛疗法的了解，为医院提供的照护制定医疗保险计费代码，并制定评估和治疗生命末期疼痛的新标准。
Annas says lawyers can play a key role in insisting that these well-meaning medical initiatives translate into better care.
安纳斯说，律师可以发挥关键作用，督促这些出于善意的医疗举措真正转化为更好的照护。
“Large numbers of physicians seem unconcerned with the pain their patients are needlessly and predictably suffering”, |to the extent that it constitutes “systematic patient abuse”.
“许多医生似乎漠不关心，任由患者承受本无必要、而且完全可以预见的疼痛”，其程度甚至构成了“系统性的患者虐待”。
He says medical licensing boards “must make it clear...that painful deaths are presumptively ones |that are incompetently managed and should result in license suspension.”
他说，医疗执照管理机构“必须明确……原则上应推定，患者在痛苦中死去是处置不当所致，并应因此暂停相关医生的执业资格”。

articles.title: 翻译 · 行为科学的解释方式
articles.context: 2002年的Part B是英译汉。这里保留原卷指定翻译的五处划线原文，去掉题号与说明。原文第四句的They指上文的freedom and dignity；末句these issues指技术由谁使用、用于何种目的。
rows: One difficulty is that almost all of what is called behavioral science |continues to trace behavior to states of mind, feelings, traits of character, human nature, and so on.
困难之一在于，所谓的行为科学几乎都仍然把行为归因于心理状态、情感、性格特征、人性等等。
The behavioral sciences have been slow to change |partly because the explanatory items often seem to be directly observed |and partly because other kinds of explanations have been hard to find.
行为科学之所以迟迟未能改变，部分原因是这些用来解释行为的因素往往看起来可以直接观察到，另一部分原因则是其他解释方式一直难以找到。

The role of natural selection in evolution was formulated only a little more than a hundred years ago, |and the selective role of the environment in shaping and maintaining the behavior of the individual |is only beginning to be recognized and studied.
自然选择在进化中的作用，直到一百多年前才得到阐明；而环境在塑造和维持个体行为方面所起的选择作用，则才刚刚开始得到认识和研究。
only a little more than a hundred years ago

They are the possessions of the autonomous (self-governing) man of traditional theory, |and they are essential to practices in which a person is held responsible for his conduct and given credit for his achievements.
它们是传统理论中自主的人所拥有的属性；而要求个人为自己的行为负责，并把他的成就归功于他本人，这些做法都以它们为必要前提。
Until these issues are resolved, a technology of behavior will continue to be rejected, |and with it possibly the only way to solve our problems.
在这些问题得到解决之前，行为技术仍会遭到拒绝；随之被拒绝的，可能还有解决我们问题的唯一途径。

aggressive: 积极强力的；过度积极的
